transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, what really scared me enough to come in is that... I’ve been hearing my name called. It happens from the hallway at home, and it even happened once at the warehouse where I work when absolutely nobody was around. It just sounds so real, you know? Like my husband is standing right next to me. So, I figured I needed to get it checked out.
Have you experienced anything else unusual, like seeing things that aren't there, besides hearing your name called?
No, I haven't seen anything. Um... I haven't noticed anything else unusual like that. It's really just the voice, just hearing my name called out when nobody is around. That's the only thing.
Have you been using any alcohol or drugs recently?
No, I haven't. I don't do any drugs, and I... well, I don't really drink alcohol either. Not recently, anyway. It's just not my thing.
How long have you been hearing your name called?
Well, this whole thing... like, going from being really wound up and restless, to hearing my name, and then just crashing... it's been going on for about three weeks now.
Have you been feeling sad or depressed over the past few weeks?

Yeah, I have. After all that running around and arguing I was doing earlier, I just... I dropped into this really heavy, empty feeling. I'll just sit at the kitchen table and cry over absolutely nothing. It feels like I just can't get myself back.
You mentioned being really wound up and restless earlier, can you tell me more about what that felt like?

Well, at first I just felt really fired up. Like I was almost unstoppable with my craft business and getting all the house rules in order. But... I guess I was also pretty on edge. I would snap at my husband over the smallest little comment. It just felt like he was trying to hold me back, you know? So I'd just get really angry with him over basically nothing.
Did you have a decreased need for sleep during the times you felt really fired up and unstoppable?

Yeah, I did. For a while there, I was only sleeping maybe two or three hours a night. But I'd wake up just... completely ready to go. It honestly felt like sleep was just wasting time that I needed for my projects.
Do you feel guilty about anything when you're feeling really down?

No, not really. I don't think I feel guilty about anything specific. It's... it's more just that heavy, empty feeling I was talking about. I don't really sit around blaming myself for things, I just feel really sad for no reason.
When you're feeling really down, do you still enjoy activities that you normally like to do?

No, I don't. When I get like that, I just stop doing everything I normally like. I haven't even touched my knitting basket or my garden beds lately. I stopped going to my book club, and I didn't even sign up to help at the church food pantry like I usually do. It just... it all feels like way too much trouble, and honestly, none of it seems worth doing when I feel that down.
How long have you been hearing your name called without any periods where the voice stopped?
I haven't heard my name called like that. I don't hear voices or anything. I just... I get really down, or I get really wired, but I haven't heard anyone calling my name when no one is there.
How often do you feel that heavy, empty feeling when you're really down?

Well, it usually happens after I've had one of those times where I'm just running around constantly and arguing with everyone. After all that energy burns out, I just drop into it. I'll just sit at the kitchen table and cry over absolutely nothing. It's like I just can't get myself back to normal. It happens every time I crash from being so wired.
How long do you usually stay in that heavy, empty feeling after you crash from being really wired?

Well, it lasts a while. Like right now, this depressed, withdrawn part has been hanging over me for about three months. It's just been dragging on... though I will say it became a lot harder to manage after these past few weeks.
How long do these periods of feeling really fired up and unstoppable usually last?
Well, this whole thing... the change from being all wound up and restless, and then crashing down into this... it usually goes on for about three weeks at a time.
Do you always crash into a depressed state after one of your episodes of being really fired up and unstoppable?

Well, honestly, I'm not entirely sure. I know it happened this time, and it feels like it usually goes that way... but I haven't really kept track of whether it happens every single time. It just feels like a pattern I end up falling into.
Do you always feel really down after one of your episodes of being really fired up and unstoppable?

I think I just answered that, but... yeah, like I said, I'm not really sure if it happens every single time. It definitely happened this time, and it feels like the usual routine, but I haven't really been keeping a strict record of it.
Do you always crash into a depressed state after one of your episodes of being really fired up and unstoppable?

I feel like we're going in circles here, doc. You just asked me that exact same thing. 

Like I said a second ago, I really don't know if it happens every single time. I don't have a different answer for you... I just haven't kept track of it enough to say yes or no for sure. I only know that it happened this time around.
Do you always feel really down after one of your episodes of being really fired up and unstoppable?

Okay, seriously, are you... are you reading off a broken script or something? That is the exact same question again. 

I really don't know how else to tell you this. I don't know. I don't keep a log of it, so I can't say if it happens every single time. I just know I'm down right now, and I was fired up before this. That's all I can tell you. Can we please move on to something else?
How long have you been feeling this heavy, empty feeling that you're experiencing now?
I'd say this depressed, withdrawn feeling has been hanging over me for about three months now. But... it definitely became a lot harder to manage over these past few weeks.
Do you ever feel really down without having been really fired up and unstoppable beforehand?

I don't think so. I mean, I'm not entirely sure, but... usually, if I'm feeling this low, it's after I've had one of those times where I'm just going non-stop. I don't really remember just waking up feeling like this out of nowhere without having that high energy first.
